blocking_issues.issue: The biographical account of the 1918 advance to Damascus and its ethical consequences omits the Tafas episode (27 September 1918), including the killings of civilians by retreating Ottoman forces and Lawrence's documented account of retaliatory orders and killings of prisoners. The dossier instead speaks generically of 'reprisals' and 'killing' without identifying this material and contested decision by its subject. BIOGRAPHICAL-RESEARCH.md requires examination of documented violent and controversial conduct, attributed and distinguished from later inference; an extensive account of Lawrence's wartime agency is incomplete without this episode.
evidence: Scott Anderson, Smithsonian Magazine, 'The True Story of Lawrence of Arabia' (2014), reports Lawrence's 'no quarter' order and quotes his battlefield report on the killing of captives, while locating the events after Tafas: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/true-story-lawrence-arabia-180951857/

Historical article published by the Turkish Historical Society (Belleten, 1987) independently discusses the late-1918 no-prisoners order and Arab Bulletin No. 106; its interpretation is critical and should be checked against the primary narrative, not adopted as unqualified fact: https://www.belleten.gov.tr/eng/full-text/1948/eng
Boston University scholarly conference paper discusses Tafas and competing interpretations of Lawrence's responsibility and intentions: https://www.bu.edu/historic/conference08/bwyattbrown.pdf
Neither locale names Tafas or provides a source-based assessment of Lawrence's conduct there.

blocking_issues.issue: The first chart is a defensible, approximate comparison of the three editions' lengths (335, 250, 130 thousand words). The second chart selects unrelated intervals (1916–17=1, 1918–26=8, 1926–35=9 years) with no common analytical population or causal variable and merely recasts selected dates already listed in the chronology table. It adds no independent evidence about the revolt's logistics, postwar mandates or the book's substantive revisions. Although the numeric chart floor is mechanically met, the effective substantive two-chart requirement fails under RESEARCH-VISUALS.md §QA gate (visually redundant/decorative research) and BIOGRAPHICAL-RESEARCH.md §Contrato gráfico.
evidence: Both locales chart arrays [[335,250,130],[1,8,9]], matching numeric values; the 1/8/9 intervals are arithmetic, not invented measurements, but their selection does not support an analytical comparison.

Jeremy Wilson's T. E. Lawrence Studies confirms approximately 334,500 words for the Oxford text and 250,500 for the subscribers' text: https://www.telstudies.org.uk/biography/biography/t_e_lawrence_as_writer.html
RESEARCH-VISUALS.md §§Evidence rules and QA gate require material insight, not redundant or decorative counts.
